thread:
Maya R.: Heads-up: we're seeing a cluster-wide uptick in NVIDIA Xid 31 and Xid 13 in us-east1 between ~02:10-02:30 UTC. Spike concentrated on a handful of A10 nodes. Trying to correlate to workloads — can folks who own the embedder/decoder flows weigh in?

Ashok: On it. Do we have a quick query to pull card IDs + optype distribution for that window?

Li: Yup, ran a fast ES/Kibana filter. Query I used:
```
index=gpu-telemetry* AND timestamp:[2026-03-18T02:10:00 TO 2026-03-18T02:31:00] AND (xid:31 OR xid:13) | stats count() by card_id, model_shard, op_type, tenant_id, job_batch_size
```
Results look like: bulk of hits from card_id 10,11,12 (rack-r2) and op_type=decode/greedy with batch_size<=8. Tenant skewed to embedder-prod and a new low-latency small-batch consumer.

Sam: I also pulled vm telemetry: those cards show elevated correctable ECC counts and occasional PMIC warning logs around the same time. Not full ECC fatal but repeated correctables before xid bursts.

Maya R.: Interesting — small-batch decodes + correctable ECCs could match a thermal/noise or power-management instability pattern we saw last month. Any hardware differences? A10 firmware?

Li: A10s on that rack are on fw 1.2.3, whereas most fleet A10s are 1.2.1. We recently rolled fw for perf on a patch subset. Patch notes mentioned a PMIC timing tweak.

Ashok: That aligns. Correlation matrix: xid31 strongly associated with op_type=decode and low seq_len (<64) workloads, xid13 more with NVDEC failures during bursty RPC retries. Suggest we triage by: 1) soft-drain card 10/11/12, 2) route small-batch decode traffic to H100 pool temporarily, 3) keep telemetry capture at 1s granularity for the next 2 hours.

ops-bot: NOTICE: softdrain request queued for nodes rack-r2-card10,rack-r2-card11,rack-r2-card12 by @Ashok. ETA 3m.

Sam: Commands I ran for diag (paste for runbook):
```
# live metrics
nvidia-smi -i 10 --query-gpu=timestamp,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,correctable_ecc_errors,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv -l 1
# collect driver logs
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -S "2026-03-18 02:00:00" -U "2026-03-18 03:00:00" > /tmp/nvidia-r2-02-logs.txt
```
Attached the small export to the ticket.

Maya R.: Good runbook. Also add kernel dmesg snippet filter: `dmesg | grep -Ei "xid|gpu|ecc|pmic|thermal"` and collect device serials. We may need RMA if corrected errors keep climbing after reboot.

Li: One more datapoint: model shard mapping shows embedder-prod pinned to A10 affinity via routing policy for latency. That made the exposure worse. I recommend temporarily relaxing affinity for embedder-prod to include h100-dedicated for the next 24h.

Ashok: Agreed. I'll update routing: set policy embedder-prod to region-fallback=[us-east1-h100-pool] and reduce max-concurrent on A10s to 8 for soft isolation.

Maya R.: Assigning owners: @Ashok to coordinate drains and routing, @Sam to monitor ECC counts post-drain, @Li to verify telemetry+search filters. I'll open infra-ticket INF-2026-482 and link to ops incident. Plan: 48h watch, if correctable ECC per-card > 500 in 24h or any new Xid 31/13 reappearance after reboot, schedule physical replacement.

Li: I've added the Kibana saved search and a dashboard panel for A10-card-level Xid trends. Sharing link: https://kibana.redwood.example/d/xyz (internal).

Sam: After soft-drain + route change, Xid spike dropped to baseline within 5m. Continued monitoring but looks promising.

Maya R.: Nice work. Follow-ups: - confirm firmware rollback/patch plan for A10 subset if we see recurrence, - add a runbook step to auto-snooze latency-sensitive routing when Xid rate > threshold, - cost note: routing to H100 increases per-token cost ~2.8x; we'll notify finance if extended beyond 6h.

Ashok: Noted on cost. I'll also open a procurement ticket for spare A10s for rack-r2.

ops-bot: INCIDENT INF-2026-482 created by Maya R. Related nodes: rack-r2-card10,11,12.

Maya R.: Closing thread for now — monitoring channel will update. :white_check_mark:
